# DAMA-DMBOK

## Localization result

DAMA-DMBOK is represented locally as a versioned professional framework for data-management principles, practices, functions, governance, and common language; it is not treated as an empirical theory.

## Core knowledge

- The framework spans data governance, architecture, modeling and design, storage and operations, security, integration and interoperability, documents and content, master and reference data, data warehousing and business intelligence, metadata, and data quality.
- The official overview emphasizes ethics, governance, integration, emerging technologies, strategic alignment, compliance, operational efficiency, and professional education.
- DMBOK is consensus-based and vendor-neutral, defining scope and foundational competencies rather than prescribing one tool or implementation.
- It is not a regulation, certification by itself, technology manual, exhaustive repository, or one-size-fits-all method.
- The framework is evolving; version and date must be recorded, particularly during the DMBOK 3.0 evergreening initiative.

## Agent workflow

1. Use DMBOK to classify a data-management problem and identify governance, role, policy, process, quality, security, and metadata requirements.
2. Translate the professional framework into testable research constructs or design requirements using an explicit theoretical bridge.
3. Record framework version and supplement it with applicable laws, standards, and organizational context.

## Limits and stop conditions

- Do not cite DMBOK as causal evidence that a practice improves performance.
- Do not treat it as a binding legal requirement or a technical implementation specification.
- The commercial body-of-knowledge text is not mirrored; the local card is based on the public official overview.
